one_star_reviews.text:
ZERO STARS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Absolutely disgusting experience from start to finish.

My son was quoted $200–$300 for the work. The final bill? Over $1,300. That’s more than FOUR TIMES the amount he was quoted.

What makes this even more unacceptable is that the shop NEVER contacted him to tell him the cost had increased. Not once. My son even called the shop himself while he was at work to ask if his truck was ready for pickup, and they STILL never mentioned that the $200–$300 job had turned into a $1,300+ bill.

Because he was at work, someone else picked the truck up for him. It was only afterward that my son found out what he had actually been charged.

How is this acceptable? If a repair is going to go from a few hundred dollars to over $1,300, you CONTACT THE CUSTOMER. You don’t just carry on with the work, say absolutely nothing, and then surprise them with a bill that is more than four times the original quote.

And unfortunately, that wasn’t even the end of it.

The truck went into the shop absolutely spotless. When it came back, it was covered in greasy handprints and marks all over the driver’s door, with a TON of greasy gravel, dirt and debris all over the floorboards. It was absolutely disgusting.

A customer’s vehicle should be treated with some basic level of care and respect. This wasn’t a little bit of dust from being in a shop — it was grease, dirt and gravel ground all over the interior of a truck that was brought in clean.

Repairs can cost more than expected. That’s not the issue. The issue is the complete lack of communication, transparency and respect for the customer and their property.

Quote someone $200–$300. If the price is going to be substantially higher, CALL THEM. Give them the choice to approve the additional work or say no. Don’t keep them completely in the dark and then hand them a bill for over $1,300.

My son trusted this shop, and they completely failed to earn that trust.

If you’re considering using this shop, get everything in writing, insist that you’re contacted before any additional work or charges are incurred, and take pictures of your vehicle before handing over the keys.

We will never use this shop again, and based on this experience, I would strongly encourage others to think twice before handing them their vehicle.

Campus is supposed to be a place for entertainment, where guests go to relax, have fun, and enjoy a safe experience. Unfortunately, our visit proved to be the exact opposite and presented serious concerns regarding client safety and consumer transparency.
A staff member led my friend to a private area without providing any information about fees, time limits, or pricing per song. After a brief conversation with no agreement in place, he unexpectedly demanded $80. When my friend questioned this lack of transparency, the situation immediately escalated into physical aggression and explicit threats of violence until payment was made.
When we reported this incident to the management team on site, they pretended to be surprised, but their total lack of action suggests an environment where predatory pricing and intimidation tactics are planned, tolerated and ignored.
Entertainment venues should prioritize the safety, consent, and clear communication of their services. If you want a fun night out without falling victim to extortion tactics or physical danger, avoid this place. Management and staff clearly does not care about the safety or well-being of their customers.

I had a very disappointing experience at this store today, September 3, 2026, at approximately 2:17 p.m.

I was trying to make a purchase when my card was declined. I completely understand that payment issues can happen, and I was not upset with the store simply because the transaction didn’t go through. What really upset me was the way I was treated afterward, particularly by one of the employees.

The employee’s attitude and the way she spoke to me made me feel extremely uncomfortable and embarrassed. I felt like I was being looked down on and made to feel like I was somehow less than because my payment was declined. A declined card does not mean someone is broke or doesn’t have money, and there was absolutely no reason for me to be treated that way.

I was simply trying to make a purchase, and I expected to be treated with basic respect and professionalism. Instead, I left feeling humiliated, which is especially upsetting because I was actually trying to purchase something special for my daughter.

I unfortunately don’t have the employee’s name, but management should be able to determine who was working around 2:12 p.m. on September 3rd and look into what happened.

I hope management takes this seriously. Customers should never be made to feel embarrassed or judged because of a payment issue. The way a customer is treated matters just as much as the transaction itself.

The Canadian Brewhouse is hands down one of the best places we’ve ever eaten! From the moment we walked through the door, we felt welcomed and taken care of.

It’s not often you leave a restaurant feeling completely full, happy, and genuinely impressed by the people who work there, but this place absolutely nailed it.

If you’re ever in the area, DO NOT hesitate to stop in! You’ll leave with a full belly, a smile on your face, and probably already planning your next visit.

Thank you to the entire team for such an amazing experience! We will definitely be back! ❤️🍔🏒

Golf Course Review

The course itself is in great condition and has a good layout. Unfortunately, the customer service and staff experience need significant improvement.

The course was completely booked, and the marshal was constantly pushing players to maintain pace, which is understandable. However, there was no beverage/food cart service on August 20, which became a major issue.

We stopped after the  9th hole and ordered drinks and breakfast sandwiches. We told the staff we would continue playing and return after teeing off the 10th hole and pick up our food. When we returned, we were told they were out of eggs and would instead make us four burgers. We were told to come back later.

We continued to holes 11 and 12 when the marshal again told us to pick up the pace. We called the pro shop and asked if someone could bring out the food we had already paid for, explaining that stopping to retrieve it would slow our pace. We were told no, and that we had to come back to get it ourselves.

When we finally went to pick up the food, it still wasn’t ready, leaving us standing around and waiting.

The irony is that we were being pressured to play faster while the course’s own food service was causing delays.

The course is good, but the staff and customer service need serious attention. This is a long drive from the city, and if customers are going to make that trip, they should receive the level of service expected at a facility of this quality.

Great course, disappointing service. Ownership and management need to take a serious look at the customer experience and provide the staff with proper customer-service training.

Our recent mortgage experience was completely horrible.

We first met with Lindsay on September 2nd. Lindsay indicated my partner would likely need a cosigner for her first mortgage, but confirmed the source of downpayment and said with her parents co-signing the numbers should be good. We spoke about a $40000 downpayment and using my partner's saving of $20000 and her rrsp as as a source of downpayment. I myself was not going on the mortgage as I am on LTD and Lindsay indicated that would be an issue as an income source. In this same meeting I asked her directly and clearly about a notice of water intrusion provided by the sellers of the only property we were interested in. I asked her if it would cause an issue with financing and she said no. I said again to her " oh okay, when I looked for my home this kind of thing was an issue, water getting the basement that kind of thing" she said it wasn't an issue.

So we got her all the documents we could except for one, my partner's payslip was an issue to get however Lindsay said everything looked good and she just needed the payslip. It took awhile but we got it into her, 4 days deep into our initial 10 day period for financing.  Then on day 9, in the afternoon Lindsay indicates that the water issue in the disclosure that she knew about a week before we even made an offer was an issue.... In the same email she now tells us the ratios are too close and we need also pay off our car loan of about $6500.

All of this information could have found its way to us much sooner but nonetheless we hopped over these hurdles. Car loan? No sweat we indicated we would pay in full before close if approved. The water issue? We payed $150 for a quote and went back and forth with the sellers for days, requiring an extension eventually securing a deal where they pay to have $16000 in work done before closing to appease the needs of the lender. We get this to Lindsay, and after waiting to hear back and having calls and emails ignored she hits us with more requirements. Then she tells us only $9000 of my partner's RRSP is available? Again where was this information before we negotiated a $16000 term. Meridian was then closed for truth and reconciliation day. We both had indicated to Lindsay that we wanted a noon call on Friday as that was a time offered. Lindsay didn't respond confirming our appointment on Friday at noon until Friday at around 10am. After that call took place Lindsay tells us she will get back with more info regarding what my partner can use as a downpayment and calls back right at the end of her shift telling my partner she can get a gift vaguely. We set up another meeting for today 10am. I tell Lindsay hey I can gift my partner $11000 dollars that's needed to make up the downpayment difference. My partner sends in one more form. Lindsay again indicates things look good and she will let us know before end of day. Well at 4:50 were both calling her and getting nobody and she eventually send us email saying we're now $20000 short on the downpayment ?  We have gone over the source downpayment 4 times.

Our entire experience with her as completely unprofessional in nature. The requirements from her are a moving goal. Roughly half of the information she has told us has been contradicted later. We keep getting a told verbally everything is good and then new snags come up that someone in the mortgage industry shouldn't be coming up with on the last day. Lindsay has ignored emails from myself and our realtor on multiple occasions. The way that she conducted herself has put in really bad position on this home purchase and will likely cost us the deal.

There was little concern from the branch manager regarding Lindsay's constant misinformation and outright ignoring email from myself, my partner, and realtor. I shocked at the treatment after having a great experience myself back when Sean Laycock worked for them. I will be closing my credit cards ASAP due to the action of this branch and would warn anyone to stay far from this location.

one_star_reviews.text:
The employees involved were **Yaz, the teller, and Mercedes, the manager.**

I accompanied my aunt to the branch while she attempted to withdraw her own money. My aunt is over 70 years old, has significant anxiety, and has difficulty hearing. What should have been a routine banking transaction turned into an experience lasting **well over one hour** because of repeated questioning by both the teller and the manager.

The problem was the excessive, repetitive, and intimidating manner.

Yaz repeatedly questioned my aunt about why she wanted the cash, what she intended to use it for, why she needed cash, why she was withdrawing additional money, why she did not simply use her debit card, why she needed the amount she was requesting, and why she had previously withdrawn money.

The matter was then escalated to the manager, Mercedes.

Rather than simply verifying the transaction and resolving the issue, Mercedes proceeded to ask essentially the **same questions again and again**, simply phrased differently.

My aunt explained that she was travelling to the United States and was taking Canadian cash with her. She was then questioned about:

* Where in the United States she was going.
* Why she was going to Florida.
* Why she needed Canadian cash while travelling.
* What she intended to purchase.
* Who she was travelling with.
* How long she would be away.
* Why she needed the amount of money she was requesting.
* Why she couldn't simply use her debit card.
* Why she was withdrawing money when she had withdrawn money the previous week.

These questions were repeatedly revisited after my aunt had already answered them.

At one point, Mercedes printed my aunt's previous transaction and withdrawal records and used her previous withdrawals as part of the questioning, repeatedly pointing to the fact that she had already withdrawn money the previous week and questioning why she needed additional funds.

We were then told that a report had to be prepared and authorization obtained before the money could be released. Mercedes spent approximately **30 minutes typing on the computer** while my aunt continued to wait. Even after that, the questioning continued.

In total, my aunt was asked variations of the same questions **well over 20 times during the course of the hour-long interaction.**

Mercedes repeatedly explained that this was being done "for her protection."

Again, I understand the concept of customer protection. However, there is a significant difference between **reasonable fraud-prevention verification and subjecting an elderly customer to prolonged, repetitive questioning after she has already clearly explained and confirmed her transaction.**

My aunt was visibly distressed by the experience.

She is over 70 years old. She has difficulty hearing and suffers from significant anxiety. Instead of feeling protected by her bank, she felt as though she was being interrogated and treated as though she had done something wrong simply because she wanted to access her own money.

1. Why the transaction was escalated to management.
2. What specific concern triggered the escalation.
3. What authorization was supposedly required before releasing my aunt's funds.
4. Why the same questions were asked repeatedly after my aunt had already provided answers.
5. Why my aunt's previous withdrawal history was printed and relied upon during the questioning.
6. Whether this conduct was consistent with BMO's policies and procedures concerning fraud prevention and customer protection.
7. Whether the treatment of an elderly customer with hearing difficulties and anxiety was appropriate.
8. Whether the manager's conduct was appropriate and consistent with BMO's standards for managers dealing with vulnerable or elderly customers.
9. Whether the transaction was actually subject to a legitimate fraud-prevention hold or whether the delay was caused by unnecessary questioning.
10. What steps BMO intends to take to prevent another customer from experiencing a similar situation.

I expect BMO to take this matter seriously.

⭐️ 1-Star Review - Daniel Carriere (lack of professionalism)

It saddens me that in 2026, people can still have experiences like this.

I recently went to 7 Guy-Dubuc in Masson-Angers because I was interested in seeing the property. When I first asked to see it by the owner, I was told to come back. I did exactly that.

When I returned, the owner began asking me questions about my finances. I simply asked if I could see the property. His response was that, just by looking at me, he didn’t think I could afford it.

That statement was deeply upsetting and, from my perspective, discriminatory. I cannot understand how someone can determine another person’s financial ability simply by looking at them.

I contacted the real estate professional involved Daniel Carriere and explained exactly what had happened. I asked him to speak with the owner, help address the situation, and at the very least get back to me. I received no response. I followed up again and explained that I would leave a public review if the matter was simply ignored. Still, no meaningful response.

That lack of accountability is disappointing.

I am sharing this because Masson-Angers and the Buckingham area are changing, and more families and people from diverse backgrounds are becoming part of these communities. Everyone should feel welcome and respected when looking for a home or property.

Whether someone is Black, Asian, a woman, or any other person of colour, no one should be judged or told they cannot afford something based simply on how they look.

I have experienced racism growing up in Quebec, and it is heartbreaking to still encounter situations in 2026 that leave me questioning whether I was treated differently because of my appearance.

I am speaking up because I don’t want the next person to experience the same thing.

People deserve to be treated with dignity, respect, and fairness—regardless of what they look like.

One of the least professional medical experiences I’ve had.

My appointment started 47 minutes late with no apology. After waiting that long, I received roughly 15 minutes with the doctor before someone interrupted to tell him he was late for his next appointment. My blood work received nowhere near the detailed discussion I expected.

Then came the part that really changed my opinion of this clinic: I was passed to a salesperson and pitched aggressive weight-loss and hormone-related programs. At one point, the doctor even joked about how much they could charge me because I was apparently willing to spend up to $10,000.

That told me everything I needed to know.

I came expecting medical expertise and individualized healthcare. I left feeling like I had gone through an expensive sales funnel with a doctor attached to it.

When I declined the program and said I would work with a personal trainer instead, I was told my “case file is closed.”

Premium prices. Rushed appointment. Heavy sales pitch. Questionable professionalism.

Do your research and get an independent medical opinion before spending your money here. I certainly won’t be returning.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing and unprofessional management at the Woodstock location.
I have had an extremely frustrating experience with this clinic. My appointments were cancelled twice in less than two weeks, both times after I had already arrived at the clinic. I was not contacted in advance to inform me of the cancellations. When I questioned this, I was told that the clinic had called but that no one answered. I strongly dispute this, as I received no calls or messages notifying me of the changes.
What was even more disappointing was the way my complaint was handled. Instead of acknowledging the inconvenience and taking responsibility, the staff responded rudely and made it seem as though the situation was somehow the client's fault. This is completely unacceptable.
The summer vacation is almost over, yet the clinic has still not completed my family's treatment. Only my older son has received treatment, while the rest of my family is still waiting for the clinic to begin providing the services we need. The delays and lack of communication have been extremely frustrating.
What concerns me most is that even when feedback is provided to management, there appears to be little willingness to listen or address the client's concerns. Instead, responsibility is shifted back onto the client rather than addressing the clinic's own communication and scheduling failures.
A healthcare clinic should value its clients' time, communicate clearly, and take responsibility when mistakes occur. Unfortunately, my experience at the Woodstock location has been the complete opposite. I would strongly recommend that management take these concerns seriously and make significant improvements to their scheduling, communication, and customer service.

I do have copies of all my kids ID's so I told the server I am her father and my wife an I verify and allow her to have a glass of wine with dinner. The director of events Conor Roche came to me to tell me that he was taking the glass of wine I gave to my daughter away as he can not serve her alcohol.   I agreed and told him he did not serve her, I as her father with her ID on my phone I served her.  He still took the glass of wine away from her.  I would not recommend this venue to anyone.  The staff has no accommodation skill at all and really don't care about their visitors.  We were planning on buying wine and bringing home to Ontario for all our family however after this treatment obviously will not expose anyone to this vineyard. TERRIBLE!!!!

Tbh pretty bad experience at this location. Came in around 7pm with my friend who is already a member because I wanted to try the gym with a free trial pass.

The guy working there was in the office laughing and chilling with a bunch of broccoli hair kids, and when he came out he was pretty rude from the start. Basically just asked me “what do you want?” I told him my friend is a member and I just wanted to try the gym for a day. I was completely fine giving all my information.

He told me that he needed physical ID, which surprised me because my friend tried another location before and they didn’t ask him for it. I asked if there was anything else we could do and his solution was basically “buy a day pass.”

Bro, it’s 7pm.. Why would I buy a full day pass when the day is basically over? Even if the ID thing is the policy at this location, that’s fine, just explain it normally and don’t act like someone asking a basic question is bothering you.

Ended up leaving and going straight to the YMCA. They got me signed up with a picture id and blessed us with free guest passes without the same headache and were actually welcoming and helpful.

Definitely left a bad first impression. If you’re trying out a gym and choosing between this place and the YMCA, I’d personally recommend the YMCA based on how I was treated.

Extremely Disappointing Experience – Nearly 5 Years and No Home Built

We signed an agreement with Whitby Grove in 2022 to build our custom home in Whitby. It is now 2026, and after nearly five years of delays, extensions, and repeated attempts to communicate, our home still has not been built. We paid our deposit and were subsequently asked to pay additional money for upgrades, yet we are still left without the home we contracted for. The timelines have been extended repeatedly, with no meaningful resolution. Despite multiple emails and phone calls, we have received little to no communication or response. Our requests for answers and the return of our money have also gone unanswered. Even attempts to communicate through their lawyer have not resulted in a response.

This has been an incredibly frustrating, stressful, and disappointing experience. Building a custom home is a major financial and personal commitment, and we expected professionalism, transparency, accountability, and basic communication throughout the process. Unfortunately, our experience has fallen far short of those expectations. We understand that we are not the only homeowners affected by this situation, as other homes on the same lot appear to be facing similar issues.

Nearly five years later, we still have no home, no clear answers, no satisfactory resolution, and no clear communication about what happens next. I strongly encourage anyone considering Whitby Grove to do thorough due diligence, carefully review their contract, and seek independent legal advice before making any financial commitments. Based on our personal experience, the lack of communication, repeated delays, and unresolved financial concerns have been deeply troubling. We simply want accountability, a clear response, and a fair resolution to a situation that has dragged on for far too long.

I went there in my late 20s and the staff treat people on Methadone and Suboxone therapies awful.
They accept clients on maintenance therapies but they look down on them.

I was bullied there by a much older woman who made it feel like highschool. If I sat at the bench with the other women, my 56 year old female bully would say things like "did I say you can sit with us?"
I brought this bullying behaviour to the staff and was labeled a drama queen by them, so I spent my stay isolated and by myself.

This bully lady had just been released from prison (she gave her daughter and her friends methadone and alcohol at a sleepover and her daughter died) and I always wondered why her behaviour towards me was tolerated. I later found out that this place receives a lot of funding for clients coming straight from prison and that they tend to favour them for this reason.

I ended up leaving halfway through my stay.
It was a shame because if they didn't make it so difficult to access my medication and had dealt with the bullying, it would have been a great experience.

We had a terrible experience with Myers Cadillac. We were in town for a wedding, when he vehicle stopped working on the Queensway. We had our car taken to the dealership after Canadian Tire said it could be a computer issue. It wasn’t, it was our alternator, which we had replaced with Myers. Our bill was 2,300, which isn’t even the part that upsets us. We understand the cost of owning a car, and had no issues paying the bill. Our first issue was with Dave, the service guy who quoted us 2,500 and when we pushed back a bit to understand he was condescending and said “well, you know.. bolts do need to be removed”. My husband is a senior foreman in renewable energy and an expert field advisor.. he is intelligent and works with tools, his push back wasn’t with the cost it was a genuine desire to understand the required services.

We agree to the service, leave our car. We had the service manager reach out, I’m guessing it’s because I was trying to use the chat to contact the dealership because their phones were down. Once he reached out, I just let him know that if they want future business, it’s probably a bad idea for your service guys to be unfriendly and rude. The service manager was kind enough and was prompt with responses.

Once we picked up our car, we noticed a Tim Hortons cop was left in the cup holder. We don’t drink Tim Hortons, and the cup was covered in oil (I’m assuming, one of the workers must have accidentally left it in the car). The issue with that, is the cup bottom fell apart and our cup holders are not soaked with old coffee and milk… which the smell has been difficult to get out.

Then, we noticed our front seat has a small tear in the leather, which was not there when we left the car. I’m assuming they didn’t cover the seats of the steering when working on the car, because the steering wheel was covered in oil and dirt.

This service for a Cadillac dealership is completely unacceptable.

Unfortunately, despite having a good family doctor at this clinic, this experience has completely changed my confidence in the clinic. I have decided to move my family doctor to another clinic. one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with my experience with Spring Financial.
From the very beginning of my application, I clearly provided my income, monthly rent, and financial obligations. I was then asked to connect my bank account, which gave them access to verify my actual income, deposits, rent payments, and other transactions.
Despite having this information, I was taken through numerous verification steps, asked for documents, employment information and references, and eventually asked to authorize a hard credit inquiry, which was then recorded on my credit file.
Only after completing all of these steps was I told that my rent amount caused my debt-to-income ratio to be too high and that they could not proceed with the loan—not even for a lower amount.
Spring Financial later explained to me that their initial system had used an estimated housing expense and that my actual verified rent was only fully considered later in the underwriting process. This is exactly what concerns me. My actual rent amount had been disclosed from the beginning, yet I still went through the entire process and a hard credit inquiry before this became the reason they could not lend to me.
I understand that every lender has underwriting criteria and that approval is never guaranteed. My disappointment is not simply because the loan was declined. It is because I expected much more clarity and transparency before a hard inquiry was placed on my credit file.
I believe customers should be given a clearer understanding of their situation before reaching a stage that can affect their credit. Unfortunately, this experience left me feeling disappointed and misled by the process.
At the beginning, my experience with Maria was positive. She was helpful and responded quickly. However, once the issue regarding my rent came up, the communication changed. Responses became slower, and several times I was told that she was assisting another client and would get back to me later.

What disappointed me most is that even after I was told that they were unable to proceed with the loan, my application still appeared to be pending rather than being clearly and formally closed. I was left waiting without a clear final update.

I appreciated the good communication at the beginning, but unfortunately, the lack of timely responses and clear closure toward the end made the overall experience frustrating and disappointing.

What troubled me most was how I was treated during this process. Instead of addressing my legitimate concern, I was told I needed to "calm down" and call back later - as if requesting a refund for a product that didn't match its advertised potency was an unreasonable or emotional overreaction. This is not how a business should treat a paying, loyal customer with a valid complaint.

To add to this experience, the delivery driver was also unprofessional during drop-off. When I attempted to explain the process for buzzing into my building, he responded with "I'm not dumb" and hung up on me. He then texted me shortly after asking the very same question I had just tried to explain over the phone.

I have text message records documenting this entire exchange, which I'm attaching to this review for full transparency. I would strongly encourage this company to reevaluate their product labeling accuracy, delivery staff conduct, and customer service training.

I cannot recommend purchasing from this seller until these issues are addressed.

one_star_reviews.text:
An extremely disappointing season, especially considering the price paid.

My 5-year-old son participated this season and, unfortunately, we were very disappointed by the quality of the coaching and the organization.

In a 45-minute session, the children actually play soccer for about 10 minutes. The rest of the time is mainly devoted to games like tag, etc. For 5-year-olds who come precisely to learn how to play soccer, learn to dribble, pass, shoot, and develop their skills, I find the content very inadequate. My son wanted to learn how to play soccer, not just run around with friends.

For a good part of the season, the coaches were young girls and the sessions were generally okay. However, when August arrived, the coaches changed and we noticed a significant decline in the coaching and organization. These are young high school coaches, which wouldn't necessarily be a problem in itself, **if they received adequate training and were properly supervised**. However, that's clearly not the impression we got.

The lack of organization reached its peak during a session where **no coaches were present on the field**. Only one parent chaperone was there, and she herself didn't know what was going on. She had to go and find someone to supervise the children and finally returned with a young boy who himself seemed unsure of what he was supposed to be doing. After about 15 minutes of very disorganized activities with no real supervision, we finally left.

I then took the time to write to the organizer, Mohamed, to express my dissatisfaction and request a refund for the last three sessions since my son wouldn't be returning. Unfortunately, instead of taking the time to listen to the complaint and address the concerns raised, he became very defensive and simply stopped responding to my messages. It has now been almost a week since I wrote, and I haven't even received a follow-up.

I find this particularly disappointing given the price paid for the season. We obviously didn't expect a professional level for 5-year-olds, but we did expect, at a minimum, structured sessions, proper supervision, and coaches who were adequately trained to teach the basics of soccer.

Unfortunately, this is not the experience we had. A very disappointing season from start to finish, and equally disappointing customer service when I tried to voice my concerns.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would strongly recommend thinking twice before buying an engine from Dynamic Auto Wreckers.

I purchased a used engine from them expecting to receive a usable replacement. Fortunately, I checked the engine before going through the time and expense of installing it. A compression test showed only around 3 bar in two cylinders, which clearly indicated that the engine had serious internal problems and was not suitable for installation.

A defective used part can happen — that by itself is not the main reason for this review. What really disappointed me was how the situation was handled afterward.

Once I contacted them and explained the problem, I expected a straightforward return and refund. Instead, the process dragged on for almost two weeks. I had to repeatedly follow up, while they delayed accepting the engine back and returning my money. It turned what should have been a simple return of a defective engine into an unnecessarily frustrating experience.

When someone buys an engine, they are not buying a small inexpensive part. There can be significant additional costs for transportation, installation, fluids, labour and lost time. Selling an engine with extremely low compression in two cylinders can create a much bigger problem for the customer if it is installed without being tested first.

Based on my personal experience, I would be very cautious about purchasing a major component from this business. If you do buy an engine here, I strongly recommend checking compression and inspecting it carefully before installation.

I will not be buying another engine from them.

The worst store in Brantford by far. Everything is extremely overpriced. Yet, somehow, that does not in any way translate to quality. In fact, the quality seems to be among the worst in Brantford. When I went the other day, almost all the fruit was rotten, even the watermelons. The salmon was marked as being on sale, but it was really at the due date; any other store, out of transparency, would have simply put a reduced price sticker on them, but not Sobeys. Even when things are "on sale", they're usually so expensive that it'd be cheaper to buy them at regular price at any other store.

To add injury to insult, the cashier had a bad cough. I know from the Hamilton location that the employees are treated pretty poorly, so it wouldn't be a surprise if that's also the case here. Food workers shouldn't be at work sick, but what choice does anyone have? Now I've been coughing since I woke up today.

The only reason to go to this store is convenience, but that's probably a result of artificial scarcity because Sobeys uses underhanded methods to keep competition away. I sincerely hope that the atrocious service I've experienced at every Sobeys I've been to eventually results in the disappearance of this brand. Out of all the brands out there, I know of not one I'd be less sad to see go the way of private equity.

The only good thing about this place is the price unfortunately… I go here every now and then because of the price but I wish there was another little ceasars in Spruce Grove with better employees. The odd thing if I was hurting my body the pain would’ve lasted but it didn’t and it only started after I ate here…. idk conspiracy theory but i’m wary. also you’d think that would make me not want to eat here ever again but I only come here to get my family food for a cheap price, they’ve never experienced anything weird medically with their bodies after eating here but idk mane. Subject: Complaint Regarding Incorrect Advice and Refusal of Return – PC Optimum Transaction
To Customer Support / Store Manager,
I am writing to express my strong disappointment with the service and assistance I received at your store location over the past two days.
Yesterday, I visited your pharmacy section looking for an effective nasal medicine. I specifically asked the pharmacist on duty for guidance, and they told me, "All of these products are effective, you can take whichever one you want." Based on this advice, I purchased a nasal medicine. Since I was in a rush for work, I did not take a printed paper receipt; however, I scanned my PC Optimum Card at checkout, which digitally recorded the transaction.
Unfortunately, after using the medicine last night, it proved to be completely ineffective for my condition. Today, I returned to the store hoping to return or exchange the product. Despite my PC Optimum transaction history being available to verify the purchase, the staff flatly refused to process my return or offer a resolution. As a result, I was forced to spend additional money out of pocket to buy another medicine that actually works.
Giving generic, incorrect advice on pharmacy products and refusing to verify a receipt through the PC Optimum account is unacceptable customer service. I request that you look into this matter, process a refund for the unused/ineffective product, and ensure your staff provides proper guidance to customers.
I look forward to your prompt response and resolution.

one_star_reviews.text:
The quality control at this location is noticeably subpar compared to other Subway locations. While other locations provide a decent amount of lettuce and toppings, at this location the lettuce is essentially just a sprinkle. The same issue applies to the other toppings as well. This is not directed at any particular employee, as it seems to be a consistent issue with how sandwiches are prepared at this location.

Additionally, ordering “extra” toppings does not actually result in extra toppings; it often seems to amount to what would normally be considered a standard portion at other locations. Overall, the quality and consistency of the sandwiches are disappointing.

More concerning, however, is the food safety and ingredient quality control. I have gotten food poisoning from this location, which is completely unacceptable. I could tolerate receiving a lackluster sandwich, but having to throw up after eating there because the food made my stomach unwell is a much more serious issue. Management needs to ensure that ingredients are being properly monitored and replaced when necessary, rather than continuing to serve ingredients that may no longer be safe to eat.

The consistently small portions are frustrating, but the food safety concerns are what make this experience particularly unacceptable.

Went August 24th at about 12:15. Was quickly sat, and the waitress was pleasant, so we ordered starter soups, I ordered the Reuben with a poutine and my coworker a scrambler. We got the soups in about five minutes which were fantastic. That was the last good part of the meal.  After the soups were cleared we were informed that the kitchen was out of eggs. So my coworker had to change his order to the turkey club. Should be no big deal, but then forty minutes passed. We’ve been at the restaurant at this point for about an hour, so I ask if I can get our food to go. The waitress goes to tell the cook, who starts berating her loudly that he was just plating it now and that we were being impatient. She comes over and says he’s plating it, but I still need the food to go as we had a flight to catch and needed to get to the airport. So food is packaged, we paid (about $85 all together) and we leave. I open the to-go and the turkey club doesn’t have fries, and I wasn’t given a poutine.

Service was pleasant, if inexperienced but the kitchen needs real work. Two sandwiches and some fries shouldn’t take over an hour. The restaurant had only one other table before us when we walked in for additional context, it wasn’t busy when we’d ordered.

I’ll try Molly’s again one time, just to see if this was a bad fluke but this left a sour taste for me.

It’s unfortunate because I genuinely had a very positive impression of this dealership when I first walked in. Unfortunately, the way this situation was handled completely changed my opinion.

I have been using this pharmacy for a year and a half, and my initial experience was honestly lovely. The two pharmacists I met with were personable and kind.

Unfortunately, after repeated mistakes over the past year, I have decided it is time to find a new pharmacy. I was once given the wrong medication dose, and on another occasion, the wrong medication altogether while on my way out of town for a camping trip. If another pharmacy hadn't helped me, I would have been left without a necessary medication and experiencing withdrawal symptoms for the duration of my trip.

Most recently, I requested a month's worth of medication three weeks before an upcoming trip abroad. I was told I had no refills and would need a new prescription, so I contacted them again a week before my trip and asked them to coordinate with my doctor. There was no apology or acknowledgment of their mistakes, and despite knowing of my upcoming trip well in advance, they never once reached out to me proactively to explain the issues and give me time to make other arrangements. I was also treated quite rudely when I expressed my frustration.

Thankfully, another pharmacy was again able to provide the remainder on short notice. Otherwise, I would have been dealing with significant pain throughout my trip.

I genuinely had a positive experience when I first started using this pharmacy, which makes the repeated mistakes particularly disappointing. I no longer feel confident that my medications will be handled accurately or reliably.

one_star_reviews.text:
I visited this urgent care unit on Sunday, August 16, 2026, around 1 PM with a painful second-degree burn on my thigh. I was in significant pain and was literally crying, and I clearly informed the receptionist that I had a second-degree burn.

Despite this, we waited approximately 90 minutes before being taken to the dressing room and meeting the doctor. Even after being taken inside, we waited another 15 minutes before the doctor came. The doctor himself asked, “Did you tell them it was a second-degree burn?” When I said yes, he seemed surprised and even commented that they may need to see the burn before realizing how urgent it was.

Thankfully, the doctor I eventually saw was helpful and took the situation seriously, and the nurse performed the dressing. The one star in this review is specifically for that doctor, who was professional and actually helped me when I was in considerable pain.

Unfortunately, my experience today, August 20, was even more frustrating. I had an appointment scheduled between 4:00 and 4:30 PM and arrived at approximately 4:05 PM. I was taken into the procedure room fairly quickly, so initially I thought the process had improved. However, I then sat there for about an hour without a doctor coming to see me or anyone providing an update.

We eventually asked about the delay and tried to get someone's attention, but received no meaningful response. After waiting for an hour with no consultation, we left without ever seeing a doctor. What was even more disappointing was that the reception staff saw us leave but did not ask what happened, apologize, or even acknowledge the situation.

For an urgent care facility, the lack of urgency and communication was extremely disappointing. Patients coming in with painful injuries should not have to repeatedly explain the severity of their condition or sit unattended for such long periods without any update.

The doctor who treated me on Sunday deserves credit, but overall, based on both experiences, the organization, communication, and patient handling need significant improvement.

Unfortunately, our experience with Ontario Door Services in North Bay was disappointing.

We’re looking to purchase a couple of garage doors and contacted several companies for quotes. We called Ontario Door Services on a Thursday, and our initial conversation was actually very positive. We explained what we were looking for, provided all the necessary information, and were told we could expect a quote either that day or the next business day.

When we hadn’t received anything by Monday, we called to follow up as we’re hoping to get the doors ordered soon. Unfortunately, the person we spoke with, Liz, was quite short and not particularly helpful.

It’s now been more than a week since our initial call, and we still haven’t received a quote or any follow-up. At this point, even if their quote came in lower than the others, we wouldn’t feel comfortable moving forward with them.

Customer service and communication are a big part of earning someone’s business, especially when making a larger purchase. Unfortunately, our experience here fell well short of that.

one_star_reviews.text:
I visited this location on August 10th and was incredibly disappointed with both the overall presentation of the store and the level of customer service I experienced.

Right away, I noticed price labels scattered throughout various sections of the store and on the floor. There were also several employees gathered at the front chatting amongst themselves rather than appearing to be engaged with customers or maintaining the store. I previously worked at a Pet Valu location owned by the same couple, so I understand the expectations and standards that are generally associated with their stores. Because of that, I was particularly surprised by what I saw during this visit. It honestly did not leave a great impression.

The biggest concern, however, was our experience with the dog wash.

We brought our dog in to use the self serve dog wash and made the employee aware beforehand that our dog is reactive toward other dogs. At the time, there was already another dog using the wash, so we were completely willing to wait and walked around the store while we did so.

The employee then told us that if another customer came in with a dog and wanted to use the wash, they would still be allowed to do so while we were washing our dog. This really concerned me. At the Pet Valu location where I previously worked, if a customer specifically told us that their dog was reactive toward other dogs and another customer arrived wanting to use the wash, we would simply explain the situation and let them know there would be a short wait. In my experience, customers were always understanding when it was explained to them that we were trying to prevent an unsafe or stressful situation for the dogs involved.

I completely understand that the dog wash is a service the store wants to provide and that there is money to be made from it. However, I don’t think making an additional sale should take priority over the safety and comfort of the animals and people in the store.

A reactive dog being placed in a small, enclosed area with another unfamiliar dog can create a situation that could escalate very quickly. Even if a dog has never bitten or attacked another animal, there is still a potential safety concern when owners have specifically communicated that their dog is reactive. It also puts the employees in an unnecessarily difficult position if something were to happen.

I would strongly encourage management to reconsider how situations like this are handled and to establish a clearer procedure for customers who disclose that their dog is reactive. Simply asking another customer to wait a few minutes seems like a much more reasonable solution than potentially putting multiple dogs, their owners, and staff in an unsafe situation.

Overall, I left this visit feeling disappointed. Between the lack of attention to the store’s presentation, employees standing around chatting, and the way the dog wash situation was handled, the experience did not reflect the level of professionalism and customer care I would expect from Pet Valu.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously, as I believe these are issues that could be addressed relatively easily and would make a significant difference in both the customer experience and the safety of the animals being served.

Unfortunately, my experience with this clinic today was very disappointing.

I came in for Botox after hearing positive things about the clinic, and I genuinely believed I would be in good and trustworthy hands. Sadly, that was not how I felt when I left.

For me, honesty and integrity are just as important as the quality of the treatment. I expect to be advised based on what I actually need, with the goal of achieving a natural and satisfying result—not simply being encouraged to purchase more units.

My biggest disappointment was with the billing experience. I felt that the focus was on charging me for more units rather than understanding what I wanted and recommending what was truly appropriate for me. I completely understand that Botox is charged by the unit, and I have no issue paying a fair price for a good treatment. However, I do have an issue when I feel that the priority becomes the amount of money being charged rather than the client’s satisfaction.

I chose this clinic because I trusted its reputation. Unfortunately, I left feeling disappointed and questioning that trust.

A client should feel that their best interest comes first. I sincerely hope the clinic takes this feedback seriously, because transparency, honesty, and client satisfaction should always be a priority.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with my experience with this company and the handling of my bridal bouquet.
The entire situation occurred the day before my wedding, when my bouquet had to be returned twice.
The first return was because the bouquet contained far too much of one colour of rose, resulting in a colour balance that did not reflect the design and look I had requested.
The second return was necessary because the sunflowers that were supposed to be included in my bouquet were not sufficiently developed. Sunflowers were an important part of my wedding theme and one of the main flowers I expected in my bridal bouquet. The company was ultimately unable to provide suitable developed sunflowers as promised, so the sunflowers had to be removed and replaced with additional roses.
Unfortunately, as a result of the bouquet having to be repeatedly handled, returned, and adjusted, several of the roses became visibly bruised. This was especially disappointing considering that these issues were being dealt with immediately before my wedding.
Someone else picked up the bouquet on my behalf, and no photos of the completed bouquet were provided by the company prior to pickup. There was also no advance communication advising me that the promised sunflowers could not be provided in suitable condition.
Despite having to return my bridal bouquet twice and ultimately receiving a bouquet without one of its main promised elements, along with visibly bruised roses, no partial refund was offered for the inconvenience or substitutions.
Instead, I was given the choice of either returning the bouquet for a full refund and having no bridal bouquet for my wedding, or accepting the bouquet with the substitutions and condition I was left with. With my wedding the following day, this left me in an extremely difficult position.
I understand that flowers are natural products and availability can sometimes be unpredictable. However, when a florist cannot provide a significant element of a wedding bouquet as promised, communication and reasonable alternatives are essential.
Having to deal with my bouquet being returned twice, losing the sunflowers that were central to my wedding theme, receiving substitutions I did not originally request, ending up with bruised roses after the repeated handling, and being offered no partial refund made this an incredibly stressful and disappointing experience.
I should have been enjoying the day before my wedding, not dealing with repeated problems with my bridal bouquet and being forced to choose between accepting something different from what was promised or having no bouquet at all. Complete disappointment.

one_star_reviews.text:
Disappointing Experience with Sandeep (Century 21) — Warning for First-Time Buyers
We were Sandeep’s first clients, and unfortunately, the experience was highly disappointing. After closing, we received a gift hamper with a $200 TV but no cash rebate, which is critical in today's tough housing market.
When we raised this, Sandeep claimed he had nothing left to give because he used the entire commission to cover his own Century 21 fees, brokerage splits, and monthly overhead.
As clients, we feel an agent's lack of existing business volume and personal desk fees should never be used as an excuse to shortchange their very first clients. We even addressed this with his manager, who confirmed that because nothing was in writing beforehand, they would not step in to help.
We are posting this feedback so no other buyers face this situation with him.
Advice to future buyers: Most homeowners expect a financial benefit or rebate to offset massive closing costs. Never rely on an agent's goodwill. Demand clear, upfront transparency in writing regarding commission structures and rebates before signing any representation agreement.
Most importantly stay away from Sandeep Dhanapala from Century 21!

one_star_reviews.text:
Having been to about ~50 different econofitness gyms, this is a strong contender for the worst one. Always packed no matter what time you go and if you want to be efficient with your time, go between 1 am to 4 am otherwise it's full. People taking multiple machines and looking at you like you did something wrong when you ask if you can use one of them while they do they other, forget about working in with most of these people let alone using a bench that is occupied just to be used to sit down or put a water bottle and phone on while using another machine. The people that come as groups are always fooling around while hogging multiple machines for too long not being considerate of the other people that need them. I feel like these people have never properly trained in their lives and think this is their basement that they can do what they want. In an already packed gym, this doesn't help.

Broken machines also take a long time to be fixed and with the limited number in the most popular ones, it makes the problems with the gym even worse. Bathrooms are closed at peak times for cleaning and the only alternative is the mixed bathroom with 1 at a time that's always full, you'll be waiting for a while there. The weights are also never placed correctly, weights are never removed from machines and you need to go around the whole gym to find them because they're all over the place.

If you have a regular membership and are picking a gym I strongly recommend you look at another econofitness and if you have a platinum membership I recommend you find another gym which is worth the extra travel by far.

I visited The Boar's Nest in Cardinal yesterday, and unfortunately, it was a deeply concerning experience.

From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt off. The establishment did not appear clean, and both the staff (including our waiter) and other patrons seemed heavily intoxicated, which made the environment uncomfortable.

I ordered a turkey sandwich and a poutine, along with an Alexander Keith's beer. Halfway through my sandwich, I noticed the turkey had an unusual, off-colour appearance. My buddy ordered a hamburger, and his patty had a strange colouration to it as well—clearly not a good sign. The poutine cheese was also clumpy and did not seem fresh at all. Given the state of the food, I should have stopped eating sooner. The total came to $25.

Today, I am suffering from severe food poisoning and feeling quite ill.

I am not one to leave negative reviews, but I feel strongly that this establishment needs to be inspected—not only for its general cleanliness but for the safety of the food being served. I would strongly advise others to avoid eating here until these issues are addressed.

Another important issue concerns additional keys. If a tenant has extra keys made at their own expense, they may be required to hand over all of those keys to building management when moving out. However, the cost of making those additional keys is not reimbursed. In my opinion, this policy should be clearly explained to tenants in advance to avoid misunderstandings and unnecessary expenses.

I would also like to address the quality of the blinds installed in the apartments. In our case, they do not function properly: they are difficult to open and close, and the mechanisms frequently malfunction. I have also heard similar complaints from other residents in the building.

What is particularly concerning is the way responsibility for the condition of the blinds is handled. During the tenancy, issues with the blinds may be treated as the tenant’s responsibility, while at move-out, the same malfunction may be interpreted as possible damage caused by the tenant. I believe situations like this should be handled more transparently and consistently, with proper consideration given to the actual condition and quality of the installed fixtures.

I had a very disappointing experience with What The Law and my lawyer, Courtney Cameron. In my experience, the fees were extremely high for the work that was actually done, particularly for something as straightforward as preparing an affidavit.

What was especially frustrating was the huge difference in communication before and after signing the retainer. Before the retainer was signed, I was contacted constantly—almost daily—to follow up and confirm everything. Once the retainer was signed, that level of communication seemed to disappear.

Courtney failed to keep me properly updated about my own legal matter. I often had to repeatedly reach out and ask for updates just to find out what was happening. There were also times when my messages were left unanswered and my calls were not returned. I was initially told that the work should take about two weeks, but due to the lack of communication and delays, it ended up taking over a month. This caused me a lot of unnecessary stress and anxiety.

I understand that legal matters can take time, but having to constantly chase my own lawyer for basic updates was extremely frustrating. Overall, I feel I paid an enormous amount for a level of service that did not come close to what I expected. Worst $35k ever spent.

one_star_reviews.text:
OPEN LETTER TO PRIME MINISTER MARK CARNEY: DEMAND FOR A PUBLIC INQUIRY INTO CMHA

Dear Prime Minister Carney,

I demand an immediate, independent public inquiry into the Canadian Mental Health Association (CMHA), its government funding, its qualifications, and whether its practices have contributed to preventable deaths.

Mental illness is a medical condition requiring qualified healthcare professionals, not potentially unregulated charitable services presented as substitutes for psychiatric treatment.

I demand an investigation into:

1. Unregulated medical services: Whether CMHA staff or volunteers perform medical functions without appropriate licensing, training, or oversight.
2. Preventable deaths: Whether CMHA's actions, omissions, or crisis interventions have contributed to suicides or other deaths.
3. Fraudulent services: Whether vulnerable patients are misled into believing they are receiving qualified medical treatment.
4. Criminal accountability: Whether CMHA executives, directors, or staff should face investigation for criminal negligence causing death, manslaughter, or homicide where evidence supports such charges.
5. Government funding: Whether taxpayer money directed to CMHA would better serve Canadians through regulated psychiatric hospitals, doctors, and medical research.
6. Police involvement: Whether CMHA unnecessarily involves police in psychiatric emergencies, potentially causing trauma, injury, or death.
7. Regulatory reform: Whether CMHA should be prohibited from providing medical services without appropriate professional licensing and independent oversight.

A psychiatric emergency deserves the same medical professionalism as a heart attack.

Charitable status must never shield an organization or its leadership from accountability. Any evidence of criminal wrongdoing must be referred to police and Crown prosecutors.

I demand an independent inquiry with the authority to examine records, investigate deaths, hear from patients and families, and publicly report its findings.

Mentally ill Canadians deserve doctors, proper medical treatment, accountability, and justice—not an inadequately regulated substitute for healthcare.

Prime Minister Carney, I demand a written response and immediate action.

I encourage Canadians who share these concerns to send this letter to the Prime Minister and demand an independent investigation.

Ugh, what a disappointment! I don't know if the team in charge of organizing the "unique" events has changed this year, but seriously, I was bored.

Very few visitors (Saturday afternoon). I only saw maybe twenty people and a dozen volunteers.

One of the buildings was off-limits; you absolutely had to have visited the first one upon arrival.

People were showing up without passes! And even though I had mine, I was brazenly stopped and asked to show it as I walked by.

Very few artists and craftspeople were present, compared to previous years. There was one singer-songwriter and a couple of other people there. Two or three animals instead of a petting zoo.

No fireworks, and only two or three costumed characters, compared to about twenty in previous years.

My favorite snack bar wasn't serving poutine this year. Another sparsely populated snack bar with burgers at $20 and up, OK...

I didn't see the shows, I admit, but for the entrance fee, it's more than disappointing. This is a park I've frequented since I was young (over 60 years old), and it's much more appealing without these boring activities.

However, I commend the people in charge of a few kiosks who did an exceptional job (the creativity site), writing a letter to be given to a director of a play in 2027.

I certainly won't be going back next year. What a shame!

one_star_reviews.text:
In April 2024, we purchased a 2022 Volkswagen Taos with approximately 19,500 km from Harbour View Volkswagen in Nanaimo, along with an extended warranty. Unfortunately, since purchasing the vehicle, we have experienced several ongoing issues.
In November 2024, the check engine light came on while we were in the Courtenay area. Courtenay Volkswagen diagnosed a misfire in cylinder #1. After extensive troubleshooting with Volkswagen technical support and the cylinder head supplier, the repair took approximately six weeks to complete, and they had our vehicle during this time.
Shortly after, we began experiencing an intermittent buzzing noise when opening the driver’s door. We brought the vehicle to Harbour View Volkswagen in Nanaimo multiple times for diagnosis and repair. Although the technicians acknowledged the issue, several appointments, repeated 1.5-hour trips from our home near Port Alberni, a computer reboot, and replacement of an amplifier component did not resolve the problem.
Unfortunately, the buzzing noise continues intermittently, and the issue remains unresolved despite considerable time, travel, and inconvenience.
In January 2026, while driving to Tofino, the vehicle began running poorly at low RPMs, although it performed normally above 2,000 RPM. We immediately turned around and took the vehicle to Harbour View Volkswagen in Nanaimo for diagnosis and repair.
When we returned to pick up the vehicle, we were informed that the issue was caused by a faulty spark plug — not one that was worn out, but defective. Despite this, we were told the repair was not covered under warranty because the spark plug warranty had expired approximately five weeks earlier, even though the vehicle had less than 54,000 km on it. According to Volkswagen’s own maintenance schedule, spark plugs are not scheduled for inspection until 65,000 km and replacement until 96,000 km.
What was particularly frustrating is that between the two dealerships, the vehicle had already spent well over eight weeks in their possession for previous repairs, effectively reducing our usable factory warranty period. We were also charged $460.61 to replace a single spark plug, which seems excessive for what was identified as a faulty part.
Overall, we are extremely disappointed with both the reliability of our Volkswagen Taos and our experience with warranty support and repairs. Due to the repeated issues and inconvenience, we will not purchase another Volkswagen in the future and will be seeking service elsewhere rather than returning to Harbour View Volkswagen for warranty work.
